segments: with honor,
and served him well, and gave him rest.
And he gathered forces, took his old father with him, and went and encamped against Iconium,
and took it from his brother Qutb al-Din.
And he also went and encamped against Aksaray.
And there Sultan Qilij Arslan fell ill;
and when his son Kaykhusraw brought him to Iconium, he died and was buried there.
And that Ghiyath al-Din Kaykhusraw ruled over Iconium,
until his brother Rukn al-Din took it from him,
as we shall show by God's help.
Now that Qilij Arslan ruled—
who was the son of Mas'ud, son of Qilij Arslan, son of Sulayman, son of Qutalmish, son of Yabghu, son of Seljuk, son of Tuqaq—
for thirty-eight years;
and he left twelve sons, [all] kings.
Also Saladin, at that same time, was seized by an acute fever;
and he died in Damascus on the night of Wednesday, the 27th
of the second month [Safar] of the year 1504 [of the Greeks],
[being the year] 589 of the Arabs.
And he left seventeen male sons,
and one small daughter.
And there was not found in his treasury when he died
except one dinar
and thirty-six dirhams,
because he was exceedingly generous;
and in this way he prospered.
It is related
that when he gained dominion over Damascus, he brought out every dinar and dirham found in the treasury—a great wealth—and heaped it before him.
And he said to a man named Ibn al-Muqaddam:
"Distribute to the nobles, horsemen, and their servants, handful by handful."
And when he began to take little by little,
Saladin rebuked him and said:
"Fill your hand!"
And he laughed.
And Saladin asked him the reason for his laughing.
And he said:
"I know
one day when Nur al-Din was sitting where you are sitting,
they brought before him a box of large uncut pearls.
And he said to me:
'Distribute {OCR?} with your hand to the nobles.'
And when I began to fill my hand,
he said to me quietly:
'If you distribute like this,
there will not be enough for all of them.'"
And Saladin laughed and said:
"Niggardliness is fitting for merchants, and not for kings."
Moreover it is related,
that when he drew near to death, he commanded a certain emir to hang his shroud on the top of a spear and carry it around through the streets of the city, while proclaiming
and saying:
"King Saladin departs from this world,
and of all his possessions he takes nothing with him except this piece of his shroud alone."
notes: Saladin died aged fifty-seven years on the 4th of Adar of the year of our Lord 1193. [Footnote]
